The mapper is in `out/transform.ts`. It type-checks and runs cleanly on the sample patient at several as-of dates, and I checked a synthetic patient covering supersession, retraction, unit conversion, dose maths and drug-attributed codes.

One thing you should know first: the schema file `riverside-doc-v1.d.ts` has **no docstrings at all**, even though the task says it documents every field. So the meaning of each status code and field comes from the field names, the sample narratives and the view spec. Treat the calls below as my reading, not documented facts.

- **Medications and allergies are treated as lists that each note restates in full.** Every Riverside note repeats the whole home-med and allergy list, so the latest counting note that has these lists decides them. A drug missing from that note is not reported.
  - "Latest" goes by the note's clinical time: the discharge time for discharge summaries, otherwise the note's own time. This is because a discharge summary's `effective` is the admission time.
  - Status mapping: `continue`/`new`/`changed` → active, `held` → held, `stopped` → stopped, `not_reconciled` → unknown. `restart_advice` doesn't change the status.
- **`status_since`** for held or stopped drugs is the date of the earliest note in the unbroken run with that status. For active drugs it is only set when the drug is `new` or was just resumed after a hold; for a plain "continue" it's left out because the start date is unknown. `status_reason_text` is the most recent `instructions` text in that run.
- **Dose:** if `dose_text` just repeats the tablet strength and the sig says several tablets, I multiply. Ranges, sliding scales and per-protocol doses are left out.
- **Problems** come from `active`/`resolved` diagnoses plus past-history entries, and history entries count as active. `working` and `ruled_out` diagnoses are dropped, and a condition whose latest entry is `ruled_out` is dropped. Entries are merged into one condition when they share an ICD-10 code, a Riverside code or the same wording. I kept encounter diagnoses (AKI, DKA) because they are clinical assessments, not billing codes.
- **Diagnoses blamed on a drug also produce an allergy row.** "Euglycemic DKA, SGLT2 inhibitor-associated" names only the drug class; the same note lists exactly one drug of that class (empagliflozin). So it becomes an empagliflozin allergy row, a serious adverse event with high criticality and reaction "Euglycemic DKA". ICD codes T36–T50 that only say "adverse effect of" give the allergy row with no problem row. The AKI blamed on naproxen appears only in the narrative, so it produces no allergy row.
- **Allergy classification is by keyword**, since the source has no type field: lisinopril cough → side effect, non-immune, low criticality. When no reaction is recorded it defaults to hypersensitivity with unknown mechanism.
- **Labs:** analytes are matched by LOINC code, then local code, then test name, with unit conversion. The same test in the same specimen batch (`accession` plus test) is one result, taken from the copy with the most advanced status (`corrected` > `final` > `preliminary`). I left out non-blood specimens (except urine albumin/creatinine), race-adjusted eGFR, and point-of-care/meter glucose — that last one is a judgement call.
- **Vitals** are all "hospital", one row per measurement time. A blood-pressure-only reading within 60 minutes of an earlier set in the same encounter goes in the repeat fields.
- **Sensitivity tags** come from keyword and ICD-prefix lists, because the source has no sensitivity field.
- **Retractions:** a retracted item's own supersessions are ignored, so anything it had replaced comes back.

`out/scratch.ts` holds the synthetic test; only `out/transform.ts` is used.
